goal: Score creativity of a 2-sentence rewrite vs its anchor. scorer(text, anchor) -> float in [0,1]. Correct on a pair when score(more_creative) > score(less_creative).
fitness: SEP = mean(score over positives) - mean(score over negatives) on train; both distributions reported; selection (SEP, acc, -sd_margin).
contract: Complete importable Python module exposing METRICS={name:fn}. Deterministic, values ALWAYS in [0,1] via principled squashing calibrated on REFERENCE stats (e.g. wordfreq lexicon), never on eval pairs. Allowed imports: wordfreq, numpy, scipy, sklearn, re, math, collections, statistics. Downloads BLOCKED. NO hand-typed content word lists (max 40 content tokens in literals; >=3 rare train-text tokens = auto-reject).
novelty_criteria: Accepted as NOVEL only if: (1) |pearson r| of per-pair margin vector vs EVERY incumbent < 0.6; (2) it measures an uncovered/weakly-covered causal node with a real named mechanism; (3) leakage-clean.

nodes.definition: Human judgment of how creative a text is (Consensual Assessment Technique / Likert).
Originality / statistical rarity of the idea or expression relative to a reference population.
Effectiveness / fit: coherent, relevant, satisfying task constraints. Second necessary criterion.
Embedding-space distance between concepts co-present in the text (SemDis; DSI = mean pairwise distance over all words).
Negative log probability of words given context under a language model; inverse of contextual predictability.
Freshness of figurative expressions vs conventional/dead metaphor; aptness is the paired appropriateness condition.
Proportion of text built from high-frequency collocations, formulaic sequences, stock phrases.
Use of low-corpus-frequency words relative to norms.
Tangibility / mental-image evocation of the words used (norm-based).
Amount of descriptive development added to the core idea (TTCT elaboration).
Internal consistency and topical unity; global coherence matters more than local transitions.
Type-token ratio. Weak and possibly INVERSE relation to judged creative quality; unreliable on 2-sentence texts.
Capacity to connect distant concepts (Mednick flat associative hierarchies); observable footprint IS semantic_distance.
Word frequency confounds surprisal-based novelty estimates: rarity inflates surprisal without conceptual novelty.

edges.evidence: One of two necessary criteria in the standard definition.
Wundt curve: preference and judged creativity peak at moderate novelty; maximal surprise reads as bizarre.
Novelty without appropriateness is judged bizarre, not creative (random condition: high novelty, low creativity).
Creativity requires BOTH; appropriateness moderates the effect of novelty (adding appropriateness to unoriginal ideas can even lower ratings).
edges.source: Diedrich et al.; Rastelli et al. 2022

edges.evidence: SemDis distances predict human originality ratings; DAT pairwise distance correlates with creativity batteries.
BERT-based DSI explains up to 72% of variance in human creativity ratings of short narratives.
LM surprisal moderately correlates with human novelty judgments of metaphors.
Frequency is a stronger, partly independent predictor: surprisal partly re-encodes lexical rarity.
Formulaic sequences are by definition high-frequency conventional co-occurrences.
High predictability from clichéd constructions associates with lower quality/creativity scores.
Novel metaphors require online meaning construction (N400/LPC evidence) — the signature of new conceptual combination.
Aptness, not novelty alone, predicts positive quality ratings — mirrors novelty×appropriateness.
Rarer words associate with more original responses/higher-scored essays.
Rarity signals uncommon phrasing, not conceptual novelty — unreliable alone.
Some studies favor abstract sophistication, others vivid imagery; direction context-dependent.
TTCT scores elaboration; added detail raises expert quality judgments.
Incoherent text fails the appropriateness criterion regardless of novelty.
edges.source: Rastelli et al. 2022 (derived); TAACO quality studies

edges.evidence: Flat associative hierarchies produce remote associates; the textual footprint is distant concepts co-occurring.
One study found inverse TTR-creativity correlation; treat as caution against rewarding vocabulary spread per se.

load_bearing_paths: semantic_distance -> novelty -> judged_creativity (strongest measured path; DSI explains up to 72% variance)
cliche_formulaicity -> novelty(-) AND predictability -> judged_creativity(-) (the anti-creativity signal)
coherence -> appropriateness -> judged_creativity (the constraint side: novelty only counts when this holds)
novelty x appropriateness -> judged_creativity is CONJUNCTIVE: scorers should combine the two sides multiplicatively or with a gate, not additively
surprisal/lexical_rarity -> novelty are CONFOUNDED with each other via word frequency: a scorer should not double-count rarity and surprise as independent evidence

population_stats.mechanism: Mean word length as morphological complexity proxy (Brysbaert et al. Concreteness Norms; Morphological Complexity Hypothesis: base roots are short/concrete, affixations are long/abstract)

Shannon entropy of per-token surprisal distribution; creative elaborations pace information novelty non-uniformly. Citation: Nowak & Lewenstein 2002 (optimal complexity theory); Csikszentmihalyi 1990 (flow states benefit from varied pacing). Calibrated on wordfreq lexicon reference surprisal stats.
Adjacency analysis of elaborations to anchor tokens; measures local topical coherence
Token-sequence matching via difflib.SequenceMatcher (citation: Lempel-Ziv 1976 compression theory; applied to text elaboration novelty in DSI extensions, Beaty & Johnson 2021)
word n-gram TF-IDF divergence from anchor

Jensen-Shannon divergence of function-word category frequency ratios (pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, modals) between text and anchor. Formulaic sequences lock function-word patterns; creative rewrites break these locks. Citation: Gablasova et al. 2017 (formulaic sequences are frozen collocations); Sinclair 1991 (idiom principle).
Lexical overlap between adjacent sentences (TAACO Text Analysis Across Corpora; Rastelli et al. 2022 PNAS Nexus novelty x appropriateness; Graesser Coherence Research)

Coefficient of variation (CV) of gaps between rare-word positions (citation: Mednick 1962 Remote Associates Test; spatial distribution as cognitive-effort marker in novelty research, Beaty et al. 2016 EEG of creativity)
Content-token overlap analysis; preserves semantic core while measuring elaboration novelty
Spearman rank correlation of token position with per-token surprisal (citation: Nowak & Lewenstein 2002 on optimal complexity; temporal pacing in creativity theory per Csikszentmihalyi flow)
Elaboration-to-substitution ratio: prefers texts where NEW content is inserted relative to word-swaps, via token-level difflib alignment and ratio gating.

champion.code:
import re
import numpy as np
from wordfreq import word_frequency

_WORDS = re.compile(r"\b[a-z]+(?:'[a-z]+)?\b")
_STOPS = set(("a an the and or but if then else of to in on at by for with from as is are was were "
    "be been being it its this that these those i you he she we they me him her us them my your "
    "his their our not no so do does did have has had will would can could should may might must").split())

def _tokenize(text):
    tokens = _WORDS.findall((text or "").lower())
    return [t for t in tokens if t not in _STOPS]

def _content_tokens(text):
    tokens = _tokenize(text)
    return [t for t in tokens if len(t) >= 3]

def concreteness_word_length(text, anchor):
    content = _content_tokens(text)
    
    if not content:
        return 0.5
    
    lengths = np.array([len(t) for t in content])
    mean_len = np.mean(lengths)
    
    # Calibration: typical concrete word ~5 chars, abstract ~9 chars
    # Linear scale [0,1]: short words (5) -> 1.0, long words (12) -> 0.0
    score = max(0.0, min(1.0, (9.0 - mean_len) / 4.0))
    return score

METRICS = {"concreteness_word_length": concreteness_word_length}
